title: Meaning in Context Practice 2
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused meaning in context questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Volunteer List

The coordinator asked people to hold Tuesday evening for a possible training session.

TEXT B - Community Grant

The grant gave the neighborhood project room to grow, allowing it to add two classes without raising fees.

TEXT C - Repair Estimate

The technician called the cracked mount the root of the vibration problem.

TEXT D - Museum Entry

The new ticket rule is meant to smooth out the morning rush by spreading school groups across several arrival times.

questions.explanation: The coordinator wants people to keep that time available.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: reserve the time
confirm that the training session will definitely happen Tuesday evening
options.whyWrong: The session is only possible; “hold” asks people to keep the time open, not to treat it as confirmed.

options.text: move other Tuesday plans to an earlier time because training has been scheduled
options.whyWrong: The coordinator asks people to reserve the time, but the session is not yet definite.

options.text: remain at the training location until Tuesday evening
options.whyWrong: In scheduling context, “hold” means reserve time, not physically remain somewhere.

questions.prompt: Which phrase could replace hold Tuesday evening?
questions.explanation: That phrase preserves the scheduling meaning.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: plan the training for Tuesday evening
options.whyWrong: The sentence does not confirm the training; it asks people to keep the time available in case it happens.

options.text: clear every commitment from the entire day Tuesday
options.whyWrong: Only Tuesday evening is being reserved.

options.text: keep Tuesday evening available
move Tuesday evening to a different date
options.whyWrong: The phrase refers to reserving a time period, not changing the calendar date itself.

questions.prompt: What does room to grow suggest?
questions.explanation: The following example shows the project can expand its services.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: money specifically reserved to rent a larger classroom
options.whyWrong: The phrase refers broadly to capacity to expand; the passage shows this through adding classes without higher fees.

options.text: extra time before the grant money must be spent
options.whyWrong: Nothing in the sentence links “room” to a deadline.

options.text: permission to add a physical gardening space to the neighborhood project
options.whyWrong: “Room” is figurative here; it means capacity or opportunity to expand.

options.text: space or capacity to expand

questions.prompt: Which detail best explains the phrase?
questions.explanation: Adding classes is the concrete form of growth.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: add two classes without raising fees
the word “neighborhood”
options.whyWrong: This identifies the project’s setting, not the meaning of “room to grow.”

options.text: the word “project”
options.whyWrong: This names what received the grant but does not explain the figurative phrase.

options.text: the fact that the project received a grant
options.whyWrong: The grant matters, but “add two classes without raising fees” directly shows what the new capacity allowed.

questions.explanation: The mount is identified as the underlying cause of the vibration.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: the most obvious symptom produced by the vibration
options.whyWrong: The cracked mount is identified as causing the vibration problem, not as a symptom of it.

options.text: the point on the mount where the crack first became visible
options.whyWrong: In this diagnostic context, “root” means underlying cause, not a physical starting location.

options.text: main cause
the part of the mount that supports its weight
options.whyWrong: The sentence uses “root” figuratively to mean cause.

questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: surface
options.whyWrong: A surface is an outer part, not the underlying cause meant by “root.”

options.text: source
measurement
options.whyWrong: A measurement can describe a problem but does not mean its cause or source.

options.text: symptom
options.whyWrong: A symptom is an effect or sign; “root” here refers to the cause.

questions.explanation: Spreading groups across times reduces the uneven peak.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: make every school group arrive earlier in the morning
options.whyWrong: The rule spreads arrivals across times; it does not move all groups earlier.

options.text: make the rush more even and manageable
reduce the total number of school groups allowed to visit the museum
options.whyWrong: The passage changes timing, not the number of groups.

options.text: eliminate the morning rush completely
options.whyWrong: “Smooth out” means make the flow more even and manageable, not guarantee that no rush remains.

questions.explanation: That action explains how the rush becomes more even.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: the fact that the rule concerns tickets
options.whyWrong: Ticketing is the topic, but it does not reveal the figurative meaning.

options.text: the reference to the morning
options.whyWrong: The time identifies when the rush occurs but not how the rule will “smooth” it.

options.text: the fact that the rule is new
options.whyWrong: Newness does not explain the phrase; distributing groups across arrival times does.

options.text: spreading school groups across several arrival times

curriculum.learningObjective: Apply meaning in context reasoning across varied original short texts and explain answers from textual evidence.
